alex: Heads-up: saw a perf regression in canary earlier on batcher 3. p99 tokens-render latency jumped to 480ms from baseline ~300ms around 09:12 UTC. KV miss rate spiked from 7% -> 32%. Logs attached.

marta: which workload shape? long-context chat or single-turn bursts? any kernel mismatch traces?

alex: single-turn gen (seq_len ~256), very bursty QPS from mobile clients. Kernel hint shows fallback to int8-legacy kernel when batch size climbs past 14. avg batch size increased to 18 in the window.

raj: can you share the flamegraph link? want to see time split between kv lookup, serialize-to-device, and attention kernels.

alex: https://internal/fg/1768214329 — top hotspots: kv eviction loop, serialize-to-device, and then attention kernel warmup. KV purge rate correlates with miss > 15%.

marta: thinking: the reservoir admit window is over-aggregating during KV churn. proposal: reduce reservoir_capacity + add a token_budget ceiling for long tails. quick config to test:
```
admit:
  reservoir_capacity: 12
  token_budget_per_batch: 1400
  soft_429_threshold_pct: 0.82
  prefetch_window_ms: 12
```

sam: also consider admit split by kv_hit_rate: prefer forming larger batches for hit_rate > 70%. For lanes with <70% hit, cap batch size to 6 and dispatch faster to avoid kernel fallback.

marta: exactly. heuristic: if kv_hit_rate < 0.7 then batch_size_cap=6 else batch_size_cap=24. Also tag admission decisions as admit_reason=kvc_hit or admit_reason=reservoir for telemetry.

raj: I'll run a micro-canary with these heuristics on two nodes. plan: 5% traffic for 30m, collect p50/p95/p99, kernel-selection counts, kv_hit_rate, and qps.

infra-bot: deploy 1768214331 to canary group 'batcher-experiment' succeeded :white_check_mark:

alex: running now. initial 5m: p50 stable, p95 down ~10%, p99 down ~18%, throughput -3%. kv_miss on canary nodes dropped from 32% -> 9%.

marta: nice. throughput drop expected given smaller batches. check cost-per-token change and tail behavior on heavy tails.

alex: cost/token +1.2% (smaller batches, less batching efficiency) but user-facing tail improved >15% at p99. overall latency SLO looks healthier.

sam: for soft-429 policy: prefer gradational reject rather than hard cut. when queue_length > threshold, start soft-drop 10% of best-effort low-priority requests and attach Retry-After with exponential backoff + jitter. record drop_reason and dropped_ids.

marta: also enable replay hook for dropped IDs so we can surface worst-case prompts into the eval harness for regression checks.

raj: action items: (1) ramp canary to 20% for 2h if metrics hold (marta); (2) instrument admission decision tags + telemetry (sam); (3) add replay hook for dropped ids and s3 sink (alex); (4) run kernel-specific perf profile under new batch caps (raj).

marta: assigning: I'll own (1), sam owns (2), alex takes (3), raj takes (4). post status by EOD.

alex: will push quick script and upload dropped ids to s3://redwood-batcher/drops/1768214329.csv when available.

sam: small note — update the runbook for 'soft backpressure' to mention expected cost delta (~+1-2%) and fallback thresholds for hard 429 if soft-drop fails.

marta: agreed. TL;DR: reservoir down, token budget ceiling, kv-hit-aware cap, soft 429 partial drop. early canary looks promising.

alex: closing loop after 2h ramp. will post dashboard snapshots. ping me if you want realtime access.
